name: auto-color
description: Color-code every workspace window automatically: tinted title bar, activity bar, and status bar per project so you can tell VS Code and Cursor windows apart at a glance. Zero setup, light and dark aware, or pick a named theme: Matrix, GitHub, Dracula, Nord, Solarized, Monokai, Gruvbox, and more.

commands.title: Auto Color: Enable for this workspace
Auto Color: Disable for this workspace
Auto Color: Reset to default color
Auto Color: Add current colors to favorites

auto-color.enabled.markdownDescription: Same as **Auto Color: Enable (all windows)** / **Disable (all windows)**. When off, no window gets Auto Color until you turn it on again.
auto-color.enabled.description: Global on/off for Auto Color in every window. Same as Enable/Disable (all windows) commands.

enumDescriptions: Title, activity, and status bars plus the tinted editor, sidebar, tabs, panel, and related UI.
Only the title and status bars. Activity bar and the rest of the workbench follow your color theme.
auto-color.scope.markdownDescription: Same as **Auto Color: Set color scope**. Use the Workspace tab to set this per folder.
auto-color.scope.description: Which parts of the UI Auto Color paints. Same as the Set color scope command.

auto-color.workspaceDisabled.markdownDescription: Same as **Auto Color: Disable for this workspace** / **Enable for this workspace**. When enabled, this folder’s workspace skips Auto Color even if the global switch is on.
auto-color.workspaceDisabled.description: Turn Auto Color off for this workspace only. Same as per-workspace enable/disable commands.

enumDescriptions: Hash the full folder path. Same folder, same color on this machine; clones at other paths differ.
Hash only the folder name. The same folder name gets the same color on every machine.
Hash the git origin remote URL, so every clone of a repo shares one color. Falls back to the folder name when the remote can't be read (no origin remote, or a linked git worktree).
auto-color.identitySource.markdownDescription: What the default (non-random) color is derived from. `path` keeps the classic per-path colors; `folderName` and `gitRemote` keep a project's color stable across machines and clones.
auto-color.identitySource.description: What the default color is derived from: the folder path, the folder name, or the git origin remote.

enumDescriptions: Derive the palette from this workspace (default)
Phosphor green on near-black
Slate blue-gray, GitHub's dark look
Clean white with cool gray chrome
Muted purple on a dark slate
Arctic frost blues
Deep teal, Solarized's dark base
Warm parchment, Solarized's light base
Olive-tinted charcoal
Retro warm browns and orange
Atom's cool gray-blue
Neon pink on deep purple
Deep sea blues and teals
Rose, orange, and gold bars
A different hue per bar; follows your light/dark theme
Creamy lavender light with soft mauve chrome
Cozy mauve on warm midnight
Neon-lit indigo after dark
Dusky rose and pine on deep plum
Ukiyo-e indigo ink with sumi gray
Mossy forest greens, easy on the eyes
Ink-black with a warm orange glow
Deep midnight blue for late-night coding
Pastel pink and cyan, mall-at-midnight haze
Neon yellow and cyan on a dark street
Amber phosphor terminal on near-black
Cherry-blossom pinks on soft white
Abyssal navy fading into bioluminescent teal

Pumpkin orange and witchy purple on black

Magenta, purple, and blue

Use the single color in auto-color.color.
Use the theme named in auto-color.customTheme (defined in auto-color.customThemes).
auto-color.theme.markdownDescription: Same as **Auto Color: Select theme**. `auto` derives the palette from the workspace; any named theme paints that fixed palette instead (the workspace identity and random seed are ignored). `color` uses `auto-color.color` and `custom` uses `auto-color.customTheme`.
auto-color.theme.description: Theme palette to paint: auto (workspace-derived) or a named theme. Same as the Select theme command.

auto-color.randomSeed.markdownDescription: Non-zero locks the palette to a random choice (set by **Randomize color**). Use `0` or clear for folder-path colors (**Reset to default color**).
auto-color.randomSeed.description: Random palette seed; 0 means derive from folder path. Set by Randomize / Reset commands.

auto-color.color.markdownDescription: Color used when `auto-color.theme` is `color`. A hex color (`#rgb` or `#rrggbb`) or a color name (red, orange, yellow, green, teal, cyan, blue, indigo, purple, pink, brown, gray). Same as **Auto Color: Pick a color**.
auto-color.color.description: Color used when theme is "color": a hex value or a common color name.

title.description: Color of the title bar (hex or color name).

activity.description: Color of the activity bar. Defaults to title.

status.description: Color of the status bar. Defaults to activity.

surface.description: Tint of editor, sidebar, and panels.

kind.description: Force a dark or light palette.

auto-color.customThemes.description: Named custom themes: each has a title color and optional activity, status, surface, foreground, and kind.

auto-color.customTheme.markdownDescription: Name of the theme from `auto-color.customThemes` used when `auto-color.theme` is `custom`.
auto-color.customTheme.description: Custom theme name used when theme is "custom".

auto-color.favorites.markdownDescription: Saved color choices (`auto`, `seed:<n>`, a theme id, `#rrggbb`, or `custom:<name>`), cycled by **Auto Color: Next favorite**. Managed by **Add current colors to favorites** and **Remove a favorite**.
auto-color.favorites.description: Saved color choices cycled by the Next favorite command.

auto-color.branchAlert.markdownDescription: Paint the bars in `auto-color.branchAlertColor` while a protected branch (see `auto-color.protectedBranches`) is checked out.
auto-color.branchAlert.description: Paint the bars in the alert color on protected branches.

auto-color.protectedBranches.markdownDescription: Branch names that trigger the branch alert. `*` matches any run of characters, e.g. `release/*`.
auto-color.protectedBranches.description: Protected branch names; * is a wildcard.

auto-color.branchAlertColor.markdownDescription: Color used by the branch alert. A hex color (`#rgb` or `#rrggbb`) or a color name (red, orange, yellow, green, teal, cyan, blue, indigo, purple, pink, brown, gray).
auto-color.branchAlertColor.description: Branch alert color (hex or color name).

auto-color.environmentColors.markdownDescription: In Remote SSH, Dev Container, WSL, Codespaces, or tunnel windows, paint the status bar in that environment's color.
auto-color.environmentColors.description: Color the status bar by remote environment.

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run clean && npm run compile
